name: Speckle
desc: Laser light off a rough surface — every point on the diffuser scatters with its own random phase and the wavefronts fight to a standstill, granulating the whole field into fully-developed speckle whose grain size is set by the pupil that collects it; the diffuser creeps, so the speckle either boils in place or rides bodily across the frame, and in the interferometry styles a loaded object's deformation writes itself across the grain as correlation fringes.

energy.doc: laser power / sensor exposure, and the load applied to the object in the ESPI styles (master knob)

scale.doc: collecting aperture — speckle grain size runs inversely with it, so high = big soft blobs, low = fine granulation

speed.doc: diffuser motion rate — boil + translation together

density.doc: additional grain fineness; low = coarse macro speckle

boil.doc: boil vs translate: 0 = the diffuser slides and the speckle rides across frame rigidly, 1 = it churns in place as each scatterer creeps at its own rate

hue.doc: laser wavelength (350 = HeNe red; try 130 argon green, 240 violet)

aperture.doc: pupil shape — the speckle grain is its autocorrelation, so a slit gives streaked grain and an annulus a ringed one

seed.doc: diffuser seed — the scattering set, and the loaded object's deformation field
